angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 2,542,784 km at 57.74 pc = 0.59 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 44066: distance 57.737 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.056), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 57.737 +/- 3.233 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 18.3304 +/- 0.3216 mas (same row, RUWE 1.49), 57.0 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 3.655 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 44066: radius 3.655 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 49.134 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.079) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 2,542,784 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 7999 +/- 243 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 44066: effective temperature 7999 +/- 243 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.047) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 44066: effective temperature 7999 +/- 243 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.047) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * alf Cnc: spectral type kA7VmF0/2III/IVSr (1991JApA...12..133S)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * alf Cnc: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * alf Cnc: projected rotation speed 66 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
